results.summary: This project is a playground for (S)VGA experiments implemented in Verilog. It drives a VGA or SVGA monitor through the standard Tiny VGA pinout, with the eight outputs carrying the two-bit RGB colour signals plus horizontal and vertical sync. Testing simply means running it with a VGA PMOD and a monitor attached. The documentation is very thin, giving no detail on what the experiments actually display or how they are configured.

This design is a Verilog implementation of the YM2413, the OPL-series FM synthesis audio chip, based on the IKA OPLL core. It accepts an 8-bit data bus plus register latch, chip select and write strobes, and produces audio either as an 8-bit parallel DAC output or as a PWM signal on a bidirectional pin. The chip is intended for music synthesis and can be used with external audio hardware. The design is notable for recreating a classic FM synthesis chip in a small form factor.

This analog project contains three low-power single-ended two-stage operational amplifiers designed in the SKY130 process, intended as non-inverting unity-gain buffers for 1-10 kHz signals. The amplifiers are implemented at transistor level and are suitable for low-frequency analog signal buffering. The design is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating analog circuit design in a digital-focused environment. The project is notable for its low-power operation and use of the SKY130 PDK.

This project implements a neural network accelerator for machine learning inference, designed as an ASIC. It is intended for edge AI applications, providing hardware acceleration for neural network computations. The design is notable for its neuromorphic-inspired architecture, potentially mimicking brain-inspired computing. The project is implemented as an ASIC, targeting efficient inference in embedded systems.

This design is a UART controller for serial communication, implemented in VHDL. It provides a standard UART interface for transmitting and receiving serial data. The controller is designed for use in digital systems requiring serial communication. The design is notable for its VHDL implementation and focus on serial data transfer.

This project is a Brainfuck CPU with a fixed ROM program, serving as a demonstration platform rather than a general-purpose machine. It is implemented as a custom processor core, executing Brainfuck programs stored in ROM. The design is esoteric in nature, focusing on the Brainfuck programming language. It includes a UART interface for serial communication, likely for program I/O.

This project includes a ring oscillator, counter, LFSR, and clock generator, all implemented in digital logic. The ring oscillator provides a clock source, which is used by the counter and LFSR for various timing and pseudo-random generation purposes. The design is notable for its combination of oscillator and counter circuits. It can be used for clock generation and digital testing applications.

This project is an audio synthesizer that generates music and sound effects using PWM and oscillator circuits. It produces audio output through a PWM signal, which can be filtered externally to create analog sound. The design includes a signal generator and oscillator for tone generation. It is notable for its music and audio synthesis capabilities.

This VHDL design is an SPI slave component with an 8-bit address and data interface, a 21-register map, GPIO, an LFSR with serial output, and a timer with PWM and edge capture. It communicates over the SPI bus, allowing external controllers to read and write registers. The design includes GPIO for general-purpose I/O and an LFSR for pseudo-random bit generation. The timer provides PWM output and edge capture functionality.

This project is a counter with seven-segment display output, designed for educational purposes. It uses buttons for input and displays the count on a seven-segment display. The design is a simple counter circuit, likely for learning digital logic. It is notable for its educational value and use of seven-segment displays.
